mainTopic: Rescuing תפילין and a child on שבת, רבי יהודה's barrel passed beyond the תחום, and rolling back a dropped holy scroll
overview: The amud continues the משנה about finding תפילין outside on שבת. אביי challenges the idea that the משנה's 'cover them' case means danger from gentiles. The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words: with gentiles one covers them, and with bandits the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון argue about how to carry them in. The תנא קמא worries that a chain of people makes the שבת violation public. רבי שמעון worries that one person carrying short distances will forget and carry four אמות, and his ruling about a son born in the field applies the same reasoning. Next, the גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can let a barrel be passed beyond the owner's תחום. ריש לקיש's answer, that water has no substance, is rejected. רבא, רב יוסף, אביי, and רב אשי then each explain the case differently. Finally, a new משנה teaches when someone may roll back a holy scroll that slipped from his hand on שבת, and the גמרא begins asking what kind of threshold the משנה means. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי challenges the 'danger of gentiles' explanation
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the משנה cannot be about סכנת גוים, because רבי שמעון's method of passing the תפילין from person to person would be even more noticeable to the gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How did you explain our משנה? As talking about danger from gentiles? Look at the end of the משנה: רבי שמעון says he gives them to his friend, and his friend gives them to his friend. That is even more noticeable!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the earlier answer, which said the משנה is talking about danger from gentiles. He points out that this does not fit the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the danger comes from gentiles who punish anyone keeping מצוות, the goal is to stay hidden. רבי שמעון tells people to pass the תפילין along a chain of people, which draws even more attention. So רבי שמעון could not be ruling this way in a case of סכנת גוים, and the earlier explanation seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: You established / you explained (the case of the source)
Danger from gentile authorities who punish מצוה observance
The latter clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with רבי שמעון. He is attacking the earlier explanation of the משנה by showing that רבי שמעון's ruling would make no sense in a case of סכנת גוים.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
In what case did you establish our Mishnah,
in the danger of gentiles?
Say the latter clause:
Rabbi Shimon says:
He gives them to his friend, and his friend to his friend.
All the more so the matter becomes conspicuous!
phrases.notes: Passing the תפילין along a chain of people attracts more attention than one person covering them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא לְמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier answer (on the previous amud) that set the משנה in a case of סכנת גוים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה's case of danger means danger from gentiles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a case of סכנת גוים the aim is to avoid notice, yet רבי שמעון's chain of people is even more noticeable. So רבי שמעון's ruling cannot fit that case.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: covering for gentiles, carrying for bandits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is incomplete. 'Covering' applies to סכנת גוים, while in סכנת ליסטים one carries the תפילין less than four אמות at a time, and רבי שמעון's argument is about the bandit case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches: When is this said (that he covers them)? In danger from gentiles. But in danger from bandits, he carries them less than four אמות at a time (and on this רבי שמעון argues).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier explanation by filling in missing words in the משנה. This shows that רבי שמעון is not talking about the gentile case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added words, the משנה has two cases. With gentiles, everyone agrees he just covers the תפילין and leaves. With bandits, who only want to steal and do not care about מצוות, the תנא קמא says to carry them less than four אמות at a time, and רבי שמעון says to pass them from person to person. Since being noticed is not the issue with bandits, אביי's question disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: It is lacking / words are missing from the text
And this is what it teaches
In what case are these words said?
Less than four cubits at a time (avoiding a Torah-level violation)

steps.confusionAlert: Carrying less than four אמות at a time in a רשות הרבים is not a Torah-level violation. That is why it is allowed here to save the תפילין.
steps.whatToRemember: Danger from gentiles: cover the תפילין and leave. Danger from bandits: the תנא קמא says carry them less than four אמות at a time, and רבי שמעון says pass them from person to person.

phrases.english: It is lacking words, and this is what it teaches:
In what case are these words said (that he covers them)?
In the danger of gentiles,
but in the danger of bandits,
he carries them less than four cubits at a time.
phrases.notes: It is on this bandit case that רבי שמעון disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by rereading the משנה with missing words added.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: reconstructing missing text in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if רבי שמעון was disagreeing about the gentile case, where his chain of people would be dangerous.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון disagrees only about the bandit case, where being noticed does not matter.

steps.title: What is the basis of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's ruling and asks what principle the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: He gives them to his friend, etc. About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is clear (danger from bandits), the גמרא quotes רבי שמעון again and asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both methods avoid a Torah-level violation, since no one person carries four אמות. So the גמרא wants to know why each side prefers his own method.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נוֹתְנָן לַחֲבֵירוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He gives them to his friend, etc.
About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the case now defined, the גמרא moves on to explain the reasoning of each side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason each side prefers his method in the bandit case.

steps.title: The תנא קמא: a chain of people makes the שבת violation obvious
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא prefers one person carrying less than four אמות at a time, because a chain of people passing the תפילין makes the breach of שבת public.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds: carrying less than four אמות is better, because if you say he gives them to his friend and his friend to his friend, the matter of שבת becomes publicly noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason of the תנא קמא for preferring short carries by one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people passing an object in public looks like an open weekday activity and lowers the honor of שבת. One person quietly moving short distances draws less attention.

phrases.english: One master (the תנא קמא) holds:
less than four cubits is preferable,
for if you say
he gives them to his friend and his friend to his friend,
the matter of Shabbat becomes conspicuous.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עָדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question, beginning with the reasoning of the תנא קמא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא's concern is the public appearance of breaking שבת.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: one person may forget and carry four אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון prefers passing the תפילין from person to person, because one person carrying short distances may lose track and end up carrying a full four אמות in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other Sage holds: giving them to his friend is better, because if you say he carries them less than four אמות at a time, sometimes he is not paying attention and will end up carrying them four אמות in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's reason, which completes the answer to 'about what do they disagree?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's worry is a real Torah-level violation, while the תנא קמא's worry is about how it looks. When each person carries only a short way and hands off, no one can slip into carrying four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Not on his mind / not paying attention

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא worries about the appearance of breaking שבת (one person, short carries). רבי שמעון worries about an accidental Torah violation of four אמות (pass along a chain of people).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic tradeoff in הלכה: protecting how שבת looks to the public versus preventing an accidental real איסור.

phrases.english: And the other master (Rabbi Shimon) holds:
giving them to his friend is preferable,
for if you say
he carries them less than four cubits at a time,
sometimes it is not on his mind,
and he will come to bring them
four cubits in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by giving רבי שמעון's side of the disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון's concern is that one person will absent-mindedly carry four אמות in רשות הרבים, which is a Torah-level violation.

steps.title: Why would the son be out in the field?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and so too his son' and asks why a son would need to be brought in from the field on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And so too his son.' What is his son doing out there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and asks a basic question about the case. This sets up the next step, which explains the situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a son may be passed from person to person just like the תפילין. But it is strange to picture a son left out in a field, so the גמרא asks what case the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too his son — a quote from the משנה

phrases.english: And so too his son.
His son — what is he doing there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תפילין discussion to the next line of the משנה about the son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What realistic case has a son out in the field who must be brought in on שבת?

steps.title: The baby was born in the field
steps.stepSummary: The school of מנשה explains that the case is a baby whose mother gave birth to him in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of מנשה taught: It is a case where his mother gave birth to him in the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a teaching from the school of מנשה: the baby was born in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn cannot walk, so he must be carried to town. That is why the משנה needs to tell us how to bring him in on שבת: by passing him from person to person.

phrases.english: The school of Menashe taught:
Where his mother gave birth to him in the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son is a newborn, born in the field, who must be carried to town.

steps.title: What do the words 'even a hundred' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה adds by saying the son may be passed along 'even if they are a hundred' people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the point of saying 'even if they are a hundred'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what lesson is hidden in the משנה's extra words 'even a hundred.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' suggests that we might have thought there is a reason not to pass the baby along so many times. The גמרא wants to know what that reason is and why the משנה still allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if they are a hundred people

phrases.english: And what is the point of 'even if they are a hundred'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the son's line in the משנה, now focusing on the words 'even a hundred'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea is taught by the phrase 'even a hundred'?

steps.title: Passing the baby is better, even though it is hard on him
steps.stepSummary: Even though being passed from hand to hand is uncomfortable for the baby, this method is still preferred over one person carrying him in short distances.
steps.simpleTranslation: That even though being passed from hand to hand is hard on him, even so, this way is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'even a hundred' teaches that passing the baby along is the preferred method, even though it bothers him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that, for the baby's comfort, one person should carry him less than four אמות at a time. The משנה teaches that passing him person to person is still better, because the single carrier might forget and walk a full four אמות in רשות הרבים (as explained in step 5).

keyTerms.meaning: The hand(ling) is hard for him — passing hurts or bothers him

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's son case follows the approach of passing from person to person, even at the cost of the baby's discomfort.
steps.whyThisMatters: The son case is part of רבי שמעון's own statement in the משנה ('and so too his son, he gives him to his friend...'). It applies his reasoning from step 5: avoiding the risk of carrying four אמות outweighs even the baby's discomfort.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ יְדָא,
phrases.english: That even though the handling is hard on him,
even so, this way is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ יְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Passing from person to person is preferred over short carries, even though it is uncomfortable for the baby.

steps.title: How can רבי יהודה allow a barrel past the תחום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה, who lets a barrel be passed along even beyond the תחום, and challenges him from the rule that objects may only go where their owner may go.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A person may give a barrel to another. But doesn't רבי יהודה accept what we learned: animals and vessels are like the feet of their owners?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה and attacks it with a known rule from another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A famous rule says an animal or a vessel may only be taken as far as its owner is allowed to walk on שבת. If so, passing a barrel from person to person beyond the owner's תחום should be forbidden, so how can רבי יהודה allow it?

keyTerms.meaning: And doesn't he hold — introduces a challenge
Like the feet of the owners — limited to the owner's תחום

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about carrying in רשות הרבים anymore. It is about the תחום שבת — how far an object may travel from where its owner is allowed to go.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A person gives a barrel to another.
And does Rabbi Yehuda not hold
that which we learned in a Mishnah:
The animal and the vessels are like the feet of the owners!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the last line of the משנה, רבי יהודה's ruling about the barrel.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that a barrel may be passed from person to person even beyond the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Objects are bound by their owner's תחום, so the barrel should not be allowed beyond it.

steps.title: Only the water is passed, and water is not significant
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting לוי סבא, answers that the case is pouring the water from barrel to barrel, and רבי יהודה holds that water has no substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of לוי סבא: Here we are dealing with someone who pours from barrel to barrel. And רבי יהודה follows his usual view, that water has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the challenge by narrowing the case: the barrel itself never leaves; only the water is poured into the next barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barrel stays within the owner's limit, so the rule of 'like the feet of the owners' is not broken for the barrel. As for the water, רבי יהודה holds elsewhere that water 'has no substance,' meaning it is not significant enough to be bound by the owner's תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? — narrows the case

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's first answer: the water is poured from barrel to barrel, and רבי יהודה holds that water has no substance. Steps 15-16 reject this answer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם לֵוִי סָבָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Levi the Elder:
With what are we dealing here?
With one who pours it from barrel to barrel.
And Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
as he said: Water has no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) plus linking to the תנא's known view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel itself is passed beyond the תחום, against the rule that objects follow their owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the water is poured from barrel to barrel; the barrels stay in place, and water has no substance according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Source that רבי יהודה says water has no substance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה showing that רבי יהודה holds water has no substance. This supports ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה exempts water, because it has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up ריש לקיש's answer from the last step. It quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה says water 'has no substance.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, one person gives flour and another gives water to make dough. Normally the dough may only go where both owners may go. רבי יהודה ignores the water's owner, because water has no real substance. So in our case, the water being poured from barrel to barrel is also ignored.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Rabbi Yehuda exempts water
phrases.notes: The water's owner does not limit where the dough may go.

phrases.english: because it has no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for ריש לקיש's claim that רבי יהודה holds water has no substance.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's claim that רבי יהודה holds water has no substance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about flour and water in dough, where רבי יהודה exempts the water.

steps.title: What does 'this may not go' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to read the phrase 'this may not go' if the barrel itself is not the issue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'this may not go'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the wording of the source. It said 'this may not go beyond the owners' feet,' which sounds like it means the barrel. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under ריש לקיש's answer, only the water moves from barrel to barrel. So why does the text say 'this' (the barrel) may not go? The גמרא needs a reading that fits.

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'this may not go'?
phrases.notes: 'This' is feminine, which sounds like it refers to the barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks that the wording of the source fits ריש לקיש's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to read 'this may not go' if the barrel is not what is being restricted.

steps.title: It means what is inside the barrel
steps.stepSummary: 'This may not go' means that what is inside the barrel may not go beyond the owners' feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: what is in this barrel may not go farther than the feet of the owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording question. 'This' really refers to the contents of the barrel, not the barrel itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is how the חכמים (who argue with רבי יהודה) speak. They say the water inside is limited by its owner. רבי יהודה disagrees, because water has no substance.

keyTerms.meaning: the feet of the owners; where the owners may walk

phrases.english: What is in this may not go
farther than the feet of the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'This' refers to the water inside the barrel, not the barrel itself.

steps.title: רבי יהודה only said this about water absorbed in dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי יהודה said water is ignored only when it is mixed into dough. Did he ever say so for plain water by itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: Say you heard רבי יהודה say this where the water is absorbed in dough. But where the water is on its own, did you hear him say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's answer. The proof only covered water mixed into dough, but our case is plain water poured from barrel to barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In dough, the water disappears into the flour, so it makes sense to ignore it. In our case the water is clearly visible on its own. The proof from step 12 does not reach this case.

keyTerms.meaning: say that you heard him (say this) — formula limiting a proof
in their own form; standing on their own

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda say this
where the water is absorbed in dough;
where it is in its own pure form,
did you hear him say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 12 for ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the dough case and ריש לקיש's explanation built on it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Dough-absorbed water is different from plain, visible water; the proof does not carry over.

steps.title: Even in a pot רבי יהודה says water is not ignored
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה says water in a pot of food is not ignored, surely plain water is not ignored. A ברייתא proves this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if in a pot רבי יהודה said the water is not nullified, would it be nullified when it stands on its own?! As it was taught: רבי יהודה says: water and salt are nullified in dough, but not in a pot, because of its gravy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its rejection with a קל וחומר and a ברייתא. This shows ריש לקיש's answer cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a pot of food, the water can still be seen in the gravy, so רבי יהודה does not ignore it. Plain water in a barrel is even more visible. So רבי יהודה would surely not ignore it, and ריש לקיש's explanation falls.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the door on ריש לקיש's answer, forcing a brand new explanation of רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Now, if in a pot
Rabbi Yehuda said they are not nullified,
would they be nullified in their pure form?!
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Water and salt are nullified in dough.
But they are not nullified in a pot,
because of its gravy.
phrases.notes: The water and salt can still be noticed in the liquid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בִּקְדֵירָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא בָּטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection of step 15 with a קל וחומר and a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה would not ignore plain water standing on its own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: רבי יהודה says water and salt are nullified in dough but not in a pot, because of the gravy.

steps.title: רבא: The barrel becomes secondary to the water
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the case differently: the barrel has a fixed שביתה, but the water does not. The barrel is secondary to the water, so it may go wherever the water may go.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Here we are dealing with a barrel that acquired residence, and water that did not acquire residence. The barrel is nullified relative to the water.
steps.whatsHappening: Since ריש לקיש's answer was rejected, רבא gives a new explanation of רבי יהודה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water came from a river or spring, so it has no fixed place and no owner who limits it. The barrel belongs to someone and has a fixed שביתה. But a barrel exists to hold its water, so it is treated as secondary and may travel wherever the water may go.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת 'residence'; the fixed place an item or person is tied to
is nullified relative to; becomes secondary to

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's 'water has no substance' answer fails, because רבי יהודה only ignores water when it is absorbed. רבא's answer: the barrel is secondary to its water, which has no fixed שביתה, so the barrel may travel with the water.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the dough case. Here the water is not being ignored. The opposite happens: the barrel is ignored and follows the water.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Here, with a barrel that acquired residence,
and water that did not acquire residence,
phrases.notes: For example, river or spring water, which belongs to no one.

phrases.english: we are dealing.
For the barrel is nullified relative to the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's rejected answer with a new case setup.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel is limited by its owner's שביתה, so passing it beyond the תחום should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barrel is secondary to water that has no fixed שביתה, so it may go wherever the water may go.

steps.title: Proof that a container is secondary to its contents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבא's idea that the barrel is secondary to the water. It cites a משנה: a bed is secondary to the living person on it, and a vessel is secondary to less than a שיעור of food inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who carries a living person out on a bed is exempt, even for the bed, because the bed is secondary to him. One who carries out less than the required amount of food in a vessel is exempt, even for the vessel, because the vessel is secondary to the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the law treats a container as 'tagging along' with what it holds. This is exactly what רבא said about the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the main item does not make you liable. The living person carries himself, and the food is less than a שיעור. Even so, the bed or vessel does not make you liable on its own, because it only serves the main item. In the same way, the barrel follows the water.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out from one domain to another on שבת
Secondary; tagging along after the main item
The minimum amount that makes one liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general rule that a container follows its contents. That rule is the basis of רבא's whole explanation of the barrel case.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who carries out a living person on a bed
is exempt even for the bed,
phrases.notes: He is exempt for the person himself because a living person 'carries himself.'

phrases.english: because the bed is secondary to him.
One who carries out food that is less than the required amount
in a vessel is exempt even for the vessel,
because the vessel is secondary to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבא's principle that the barrel is secondary to the water.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a container is secondary to its contents.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about carrying a living person on a bed and carrying less than a שיעור of food in a vessel on שבת.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects from the caravan ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites רבי יהודה: in a caravan, people may pass a barrel from one to another. This implies that outside a caravan it is not allowed, which seems to contradict רבא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: רבי יהודה says that in a caravan, a person may give a barrel to his friend, and his friend to his friend. In a caravan, yes. But not in a caravan, no?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבא's explanation. He uses a ברייתא that seems to limit passing the barrel to a caravan only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the barrel follows the water, so it should be allowed to move wherever the water may go, in any setting. But the ברייתא mentions a caravan specifically. That suggests that outside a caravan, passing the barrel is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Rabbi Yehuda says: In a caravan,
a person may give a barrel to his friend
and his friend to his friend.
In a caravan, yes,
but not in a caravan, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading, which was just supported, using a precise inference from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the barrel may go wherever the water goes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows passing a barrel only in a caravan. The implied inference is that outside a caravan it is forbidden, against רבא's general leniency.

steps.title: רב יוסף: our משנה is also about a caravan
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers his own objection. Our משנה is also speaking about a caravan, where the חכמים were lenient because water is scarce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: When we learned it in our משנה too, we learned it about a caravan.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction. He limits our משנה to the same caravan setting as the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא shows that רב יוסף drops רבא's explanation, which allowed the barrel outside a caravan. Instead he reads our משנה as a caravan case too. Now both sources allow the barrel only in a caravan, where there is special need for water.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
When we learned it in our mishna too,
we learned it about a caravan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's own objection by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): our משנה is set in a caravan.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to allow passing the barrel in any setting, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה, like the ברייתא, speaks only about a caravan.

steps.title: אביי: the caravan is a bigger leniency
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is no need to limit our משנה to a caravan. In a caravan, the barrel may be passed even if both the barrel and the water acquired שביתה. Outside a caravan, it is allowed only when the barrel acquired שביתה and the water did not, which is the case of our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In a caravan, it is allowed even if the barrel acquired שביתה and the water acquired שביתה. Not in a caravan, it is the case where the barrel acquired שביתה and the water did not acquire שביתה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to רב יוסף's objection. He explains that the two sources are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's caravan case is a bigger leniency: both the barrel and the water have a fixed place, yet passing is still allowed because of the travelers' need. Our משנה, outside a caravan, is the easier case that רבא described: only the barrel has a fixed place, so it follows the water. So the ברייתא's 'only in a caravan' refers to its own harder case, and רבא's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where something 'rests' for שבת, which sets its תחום

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the barrel follows the water. רב יוסף: our משנה is a caravan case. אביי: in a caravan even both may be moved; outside a caravan, only when the water did not acquire שביתה.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say that outside a caravan the barrel may never be moved. He says it may be moved only in the specific case where the water has no fixed שביתה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In a caravan, even a barrel that acquired residence
and water that acquired residence may be moved.
Not in a caravan,
it is allowed when the barrel acquired residence
and the water did not acquire residence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב יוסף's. It keeps רבא's reading of our משנה without limiting it to a caravan.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: the caravan ברייתא and our משנה deal with different levels of שביתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies that outside a caravan the barrel may never be passed, so our משנה must be a caravan case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's caravan case allows even a barrel and water that both acquired שביתה. Our משנה, outside a caravan, is the case where only the barrel acquired שביתה, just as רבא explained.

steps.title: רב אשי: the barrel and the water are both ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the problem by saying the case is about an ownerless barrel and ownerless water. He says the חכמים who argue with רבי יהודה are רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that ownerless objects acquire שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Here we are dealing with a barrel that belongs to no one and water that belongs to no one. Who are the חכמים who 'said to him'? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that ownerless objects acquire a שבת residence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer, different from רבא, רב יוסף, and אביי. He says nobody owns the barrel or the water at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier answers assumed the barrel or water belonged to someone. רב אשי says both are הפקר. רבי יהודה holds that ownerless objects do not acquire שביתה, so they may be passed along freely. The opinion that argues with him ('they said to him') is רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that even ownerless things get a fixed place (שביתה) when שבת begins, so they may not be moved beyond their limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquire a שבת residence (a fixed home base that limits where they may be carried)
We are dealing with (defining the case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that ownerless objects have no limits. According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, an ownerless object still acquires שביתה where it rests when שבת begins.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Here we are dealing with an ownerless barrel
and we are dealing with ownerless water.
And who is meant by 'they said to him'?
It is Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן בן נורי is the one behind the view of the Sages who disagree with רבי יהודה in the משנה.

phrases.english: who said: ownerless objects acquire residence.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הָכָא בְּחָבִית דְּהֶפְקֵר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth way to explain the משנה, after רבא, רב יוסף, and אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (ownerless objects) and identifying the opposing opinion as a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel and water belong to owners, and the case depends on whose שביתה applies.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the barrel and the water are הפקר. The חכמים follow רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who gives ownerless objects a שביתה.

steps.title: What does 'the feet of the owners' mean if there are no owners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can speak of 'the feet of the owners' if the barrel and water are ownerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'this may not go farther than the feet of its owners'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a wording problem in רב אשי's answer. It is setting up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nobody owns the barrel and water, the words 'its owners' in the משנה do not seem to fit. The גמרא needs to explain the wording so that it matches רב אשי's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The feet of the owners; how far the owners may walk

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'this may not go'
'farther than the feet of the owners'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי לֹא תְּהַלֵּךְ זוֹ יוֹתֵר מֵרַגְלֵי הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב אשי's case against the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase 'the feet of the owners' fits a case where there are no owners.

steps.title: It means like objects that have owners
steps.stepSummary: The phrase means that these ownerless items may not travel farther than owned objects may travel. Like owned objects, they are limited by their שביתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These may not go farther than vessels that have owners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wording: 'the feet of the owners' is a comparison. Ownerless objects are limited just like owned objects are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Owned objects are limited to their owners' boundaries. The חכמים are saying that ownerless objects are no freer than owned objects, because they also have a fixed שביתה. This keeps רב אשי's case and the משנה's wording consistent.
steps.whatToRemember: The barrel case was explained several ways. ריש לקיש's 'water has no substance' was rejected. רבא: the barrel acquired שביתה but the water did not, so the barrel is secondary to the water. רב יוסף: our משנה is about a caravan. אביי defends רבא: a caravan allows even a barrel and water that both acquired שביתה, while outside a caravan only רבא's case is allowed. רב אשי: both are ownerless, and the opposing חכמים are רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: These may not go
farther than vessels that have owners.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְהַלְּכוּ אֵלּוּ יוֹתֵר מִכֵּלִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם בְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The feet of the owners' is a comparison: ownerless items are limited just like owned items.

steps.title: New משנה: a scroll rolls off a threshold
steps.stepSummary: Someone reading a holy scroll on a threshold drops it, but keeps hold of one end. He may roll it back to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone was reading a scroll on a threshold, and the scroll rolled out of his hand, he may roll it back to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. A person reading a holy scroll on שבת drops it from a threshold, and he may roll it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll rolled toward the public domain, but he is still holding one end. Since part of it never left his hand, rolling it back is not treated as carrying it in from another domain.

keyTerms.meaning: He rolls it back to himself

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one was reading a book on the threshold
and the book rolled from his hand,
phrases.notes: One end remains in his hand.

phrases.english: he rolls it back to himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scroll that rolls from a threshold while one end is still in hand may be rolled back.

steps.title: A scroll rolls off a roof: the ten-handbreadth line
steps.stepSummary: A scroll falls from a roof. If it has not yet come within ten טפחים of the ground, he may roll it back. Once it comes within ten טפחים, he may only turn it face-down.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was reading on top of a roof and the scroll rolled out of his hand: as long as it has not come within ten handbreadths of the ground, he rolls it back. Once it has come within ten handbreadths, he turns it over onto its writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case, a scroll hanging down from a roof. It sets ten טפחים above the ground as the dividing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above ten טפחים, the scroll is not yet in the public domain, so he may roll it back. Within ten טפחים, it is treated as having reached the public domain, so the חכמים forbid pulling it back. Instead he turns it writing-side down, so the holy writing is not left exposed in a disrespectful way.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths; the height that marks the public domain zone
He turns it over onto its writing (face-down)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Reached ten handbreadths' means it came within ten טפחים of the ground. It does not mean it fell ten טפחים from the roof.

phrases.english: If he was reading on top of the roof
and the book rolled from his hand,
as long as it has not reached within ten handbreadths,
he rolls it back to himself.
Once it has reached within ten handbreadths,
he turns it over onto the writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה, adding the ten-טפחים limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Above ten טפחים, he may roll it back. Within ten טפחים, he may only turn it face-down.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: allowed as long as it is not touching the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is more lenient. He allows rolling it back as long as the scroll has not actually landed on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even if it is only a needle's breadth above the ground, he rolls it back to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and allows rolling it back even within ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion, coming within ten טפחים is enough to forbid it. רבי יהודה moves the line down to the ground itself: as long as there is even a tiny gap, it has not truly come to rest in the public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: The width of a needle; a tiny amount

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if it is removed from the ground
only a needle's breadth,
he rolls it back to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין מְסוּלָּק מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ten-טפחים rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may roll it back as long as it is not resting on the ground.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: allowed even on the ground, because holy writings come first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון allows rolling it back even if the scroll is lying on the ground. A rabbinic שבות does not stand in the way of protecting holy writings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if it is on the ground itself, he rolls it back to himself. For no rabbinic שבת restriction stands in the way of holy writings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the most lenient opinion and explains why. Rabbinic restrictions give way to protecting holy writings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he is still holding one end, rolling it back is only a rabbinic prohibition (a שבות), not a Torah prohibition. רבי שמעון holds that the honor of כתבי הקודש overrides a שבות, so it does not matter how far down the scroll is.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic restriction made to protect the restful nature of שבת
Stands in the way of; overrides

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels in this משנה. תנא קמא: he may roll it back only above ten טפחים. רבי יהודה: until it touches the ground. רבי שמעון: even on the ground, because a שבות gives way to כתבי הקודש.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון's reasoning shows that the whole debate is about a rabbinic prohibition. It also sets out a principle that the honor of holy writings can override rabbinic restrictions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if it is on the ground itself,
he rolls it back to himself,
for you have nothing prohibited because of a rabbinic restriction
that stands in the way of sacred writings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בָּאָרֶץ עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The most lenient view, with a stated reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may roll it back even from the ground, because a שבות does not override the honor of כתבי הקודש.

steps.title: What kind of threshold is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking what kind of threshold (אִיסְקוּפָּה) the משנה means in the case of the dropped scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This threshold in the משנה, what exactly is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It asks for the exact setup of the 'threshold' in the first case of the scroll.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halacha of rolling the scroll back depends on which domains are involved. A threshold can have different statuses on שבת: it can be a רשות היחיד, a כרמלית, and so on. So before we can understand the משנה's ruling, we have to know what kind of threshold we are dealing with.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion and analysis of the משנה
Threshold or doorstep at the entrance of a house
"What is the case?": a request to define the exact situation

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: This is where the גמרא starts discussing the משנה.

phrases.english: This threshold, what are its circumstances?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the משנה's case of reading a scroll on a threshold (Step 25).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the משנה (Steps 25-28) into the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the domain status of the threshold, and of the area in front of it, in the משנה's case?

steps.title: First suggestion: a private-domain threshold facing a public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the threshold is a רשות היחיד with a רשות הרבים in front of it. In that case, the משנה would be teaching that we do not make a גזירה out of fear that the scroll will fall completely and he will carry it in.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the threshold is a רשות היחיד and a רשות הרבים lies in front of it, then the משנה is teaching that we do not make a decree out of fear that the whole scroll might fall out of his hand and he will come to bring it in from the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer with the word אִילֵּימָא ("if you say"). This is a setup: the גמרא tests this suggestion on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the end he is still holding is in a רשות היחיד and the rest of the scroll hangs into a רשות הרבים. Rolling it back is allowed because he never let go. The new point would be that חכמים did not forbid this out of worry that the scroll might fall fully into the street and he would then carry it in, which is a real Torah-level prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say": introduces a suggestion that usually gets challenged

steps.confusionAlert: The word אִילֵּימָא signals that this is NOT the גמרא's final answer. It is a trial suggestion that the גמרא is about to question, so don't lock it in as the conclusion.

phrases.english: If you say the threshold is a private domain
phrases.notes: The גמרא is trying out a first suggestion here.

phrases.english: and a public domain is in front of it,
phrases.notes: The rest of the scroll would be hanging into the public street.

phrases.english: and [the משנה teaches that] we do not issue a decree
phrases.notes: This would be the new point of the משנה.

phrases.english: lest it fall [completely] and he come to bring it in.
phrases.notes: The feared outcome: carrying from רשות הרבים to רשות היחיד, which is a Torah-level מלאכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אִיסְקוּפָּה רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְקָמָה רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first, tentative answer to the question of Step 29. It sets up a challenge that will follow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentatively: the threshold is a רשות היחיד facing a רשות הרבים, and the משנה's chiddush is that there is no גזירה against rolling it back out of fear the scroll might fall completely.
